long_biography.plain_text:
A transatlantic apprenticeship shaped Remo Ruffini's approach to fashion. He began in his father's American clothing business, returned to Italy and built New England Company around a preppy sportswear aesthetic. The family platform gave him industry experience and access, but the brand he later made central to his fortune was separately acquired.

Ruffini bought Moncler in 2003 and shifted its down jacket from technical mountain wear toward contemporary luxury. He refined the product, created single-brand boutiques and brought the company to Milan's stock exchange a decade later. Stone Island subsequently joined the group, extending the same emphasis on materials and technical clothing. Ruffini handed the chief-executive role to Bartolomeo Rongone in 2026, remaining executive chair and creative director. His economic interest is held through corporate vehicles; Moncler's stores, inventory, cash and valuation remain company assets.

uncertainties.detail: The source record and some older pages call Ruffini chairman and CEO. Bartolomeo Rongone became chief executive on 1 April 2026; Ruffini is now executive chair with continuing strategic and creative responsibility. The dossier uses the current official title.

Ruffini wholly owns RPH, which owned 78.055% of Double R at 31 December 2025; Double R held 18.2% of Moncler. Moncler identifies Ruffini as de facto controller, but Double R's full stake is not the same as Ruffini's direct personal economic percentage because LVMH also owns part of Double R.

The existing biography's 19.3% statement is outdated and collapses the holding chain. Forbes rounds Ruffini's current economic stake to 15%, while Moncler's audited disclosures give the precise vehicle relationships and group-level holding. The corrected biography avoids a volatile percentage.

Ruffini did not inherit Moncler and materially created the value of his core stake through acquisition and transformation. His father's and mother's apparel businesses supplied substantial sector experience and access, so Self-made — advantaged start is more precise than either inheritance or an independent start.

Moncler predates Ruffini by decades. Although he founded earlier apparel businesses, he acquired the principal wealth-producing company and remains its active executive chair and creative director; Operator therefore fits better than Founder or passive investor.

Moncler's market capitalisation, brand value, revenue, stores, inventory, cash, debt, intellectual property and transaction values are corporate metrics and assets. Ruffini's private wealth is linked to his direct and indirect shares and holding-company interests, not the group's entire enterprise value.

The existing Wikipedia profile matches Ruffini. No verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram or personal website met the acceptance threshold; only the dedicated Forbes profile and official current Moncler board page are proposed.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, irrelevant private-family detail and all private-vessel research were excluded. None contributes to the identity, classification or biography claims.
